title: Windows: Store "gui.console_open" in the Windows registry
description:
This removes the last dependency of the logging subsystem on the
preferences module. The latter is started much later than the former
and this is an issue.

The Windows-only preference "gui.console_open" is stored in the
registry as HKEY_LOCAL_USER\Software\Wireshark\ConsoleOpen. The semantics
are exactly the same. The preference is read by the logging subsystem
for initialization and then again by the preferences (read/write) so
the user can configure it as before.

The code to store the preference also in the preferences file was
kept, for backward compatibility and because it is not incompatible
with using the Registry concurrently.

The elimination of the prefs dependency also allows moving the Windows
console logic to wsutil and add the functionality to wslog directly,
thereby eliminating the superfluous Wireshark/Logray custom log handler.

To be able to read the ws_log_console_open global variable from
libwireshark it becomes necessary to add a new export macro
symbol called WSUTIL_EXPORT.

Grumble forgot to change the registry key in wslog.c. OpenConsole -> ConsoleOpen. Didn't notice because I had both keys present. Will push a fix.
Done in !8482.

We should probably remove `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Wireshark\OpenConsole` in `packaging/nsis/uninstall-{wireshark,logray}.nsi` and add a [RemoveRegistryKey](https://wixtoolset.org/documentation/manual/v3/xsd/wix/removeregistrykey.html) element to the WiX config.

Fine with me but I believe the references I found online do not recommend that. I believe the uninstall process should only clean keys created during installation (but don't quote me on that).

And since the installer runs with Administrative privilege (?), I'm not sure how well that will work either.

Maybe we should just add a simple parser for the preferences file in wslog.c. I thought it might be slowish and hacky.

The registry is an efficient native solution but there's no escaping that it is a deeply flawed concept.
